title: GPU slice hourly eddy archive - capacity digest
content:
PURPOSE
Quick archival export of hourly slice-level occupancy (the "eddy" series) for the last 36 hours. This file is intended for ad-hoc analysis:
- spot short-lived microbursts that don't appear in daily rollups
- correlate queue growth to specific pools and job classes
- feed into short-term reservation tuning (next 24-72h)

SUMMARY (topline)
- Period covered: 2026-12-19T00:00Z -> 2026-12-20T11:00Z (36 hours)
- Primary observation: repeated sub-hour spikes on cluster-east-3 / pool-science-priority between 02:40-03:20 UTC and again 09:15-09:40 UTC on 2026-12-20.
- Average slice occupancy (weighted by slot size): 58% (median 52%).
- 95th percentile occupancy during bursts reached 94% on A100 slices in priority pools.
- Notable queueing: short queues (4-18 requests) persisted for 18 minutes during the 02:40 UTC event. Ticketed as INFRA-9123 (linked).

KEY METRICS (definitions)
- util_percent: active CUDA SM utilization estimate derived from agent telemetry (approx; see methodology).
- active_slices: number of slices in use (distinct slice ids with >0 active processes).
- queued_requests: requests in queue for that pool/slot_type at sample time.
- avg_latency_ms: p95 response time for generation calls routed to those slices (ms).

SAMPLE ROWS (CSV-ish)
cluster,pool,slot_type,hour_utc,util_percent,active_slices,queued_requests,avg_latency_ms,notes
cluster-east-3,science-priority,A100,2026-12-19T02:00,45,38,2,28,baseline
cluster-east-3,science-priority,A100,2026-12-20T02:40,88,62,12,178,short spike - batch-job wave
cluster-east-3,science-priority,A100,2026-12-20T02:50,92,64,16,252,queue buildup - INFRA-9123
cluster-west-1,default,rtx6000,2026-12-20T09:00,36,18,0,34,steady
cluster-west-1,default,rtx6000,2026-12-20T09:20,78,44,6,146,mid-morning flurry
cluster-apac-2,burst,mi100,2026-12-20T03:00,22,12,0,52,low usage window

FULL EXPORT NOTES
- This export is sampled at 10-minute granularity; each row represents the 10-minute sample closest to the hour listed (rounded down).
- Derived metrics use agent-sampled counters (SM active cycles, mem_used) with a lightweight smoothing window (3-sample ema) to reduce telemetry jitter for single-slice readings.
- For pools with mixed slot types we include separate rows per slot_type.

ANOMALY CALL-OUTS
1) 02:40-03:00 UTC (cluster-east-3 / science-priority / A100) - Pattern: sudden ramp from 40% -> 92% util over ~8 minutes; p95 latency spike to >240ms; queued requests rose to 16.
- Suspected cause: a tight-batched training eval job (large prompt batches) from team data-science.
- Action: SE assigned (Diego) to ask DS team to move to dedicated-dedicated or fragment with concurrency cap.
2) 09:15-09:40 UTC (cluster-west-1 / default / rtx6000) - Pattern: two short 10-min bursts spaced 15 minutes apart; util at 75-80%; latency p95 120-160ms.
- Notes: corresponds to customer sandbox churn (support ticket CS-2040).

QUICK RECOMMENDATIONS (operational)
- Add a temporary reservation slice (2 x A100) to pool science-priority for next 48 hours to dampen spill and reduce tail latency while DS refactors the job.
- Lower default burst concurrency for sandbox-facing default pools from 10 -> 6 for 24 hours to reduce microburst amplification.
- Schedule job-level probing to capture per-job token counts aligned with these spikes (ticket created: INFRA-9140).

METHODS / METRIC COMPUTATION
- util_percent = clamp(100 * ema(SM_active_cycles / SM_total_cycles), 0, 100).
- active_slices = count(slice_id where processes>0 in sample window).
- queued_requests fetched from pool-agent queue length metric (approx 1s sampling aggregated by window).
- avg_latency_ms computed as p95 from trace-sampler for requests routed to the (cluster,pool,slot_type) in the sample window.

QUERIES USED (for reproducibility)
- BigQuery snippet (approx):
  SELECT cluster, pool, slot_type, TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(sample_ts, MINUTE, 10) as hour_utc,
  AVG(util_est) as util_percent, COUNT(DISTINCT slice_id) as active_slices, MAX(queue_len) as queued_requests, APPROX_QUANTILES(latency_ms, 20)[OFFSET(19)] as avg_latency_ms
  FROM infra.gpu_slice_telemetry
  WHERE sample_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-12-19T00:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-12-20T11:00:00Z')
  GROUP BY cluster, pool, slot_type, hour_utc

DASHBOARDS / VISUAL REFERENCES
- Short-term eddy viz (internal): https://redwood-ops/dashboards/eddy-hourly (scrubbed)
- Long-run daily rollup: see Confluence Capacity-Playbook-2026 -> "Daily Fleet Baselines"

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- Is the telemetry smoothing masking sub-minute thrash? Need 1-min resolution export for cluster-east-3 window.
- Investigate correlation with preemptible reclaim events (APAC had a small flurry at 03:10 UTC).
- Confirm whether these spikes coincide with any release jobs (CI/CD) — slack thread #infra-bursts referenced but no definitive link yet.

ACTIONS / OWNERS
- Diego Morales: reach out to data-science (DS) owners, schedule capacity-reservation request (INFRA-9123) — due 2026-12-21 18:00Z.
- Priya Shah: flip sandbox concurrency cap to 6 temporarily and monitor 6-hour moving avg.
- Evan Liu: run 1-min resolution replay for cluster-east-3 02:30-03:10 window and drop in /tmp for deeper analysis.

RAW CSV ATTACHMENT (base64 removed; sheet exported to Drive table): see linked artifact (Confluence) for the full export.

END.
